description: Reference figures transcribed from MScEng.pdf Chapter 4. Produced on the original hardware described in section 4.1.4, not by this checkout. See SOURCE.md. Numeric rows are verbatim; captions are descriptive summaries written for this index, not quotations of the thesis captions.

tables.caption: Kellgren-Lawrence grade distribution of the original X-ray corpus, before pairing with MRI.
Kellgren-Lawrence grade distribution of the paired multimodal cohort, by split. Splits are subject-disjoint.
Training hyperparameters. Transcribed selectively: each row records the locus in MScEng.pdf that states the value, and entries the text does not state are omitted rather than guessed.
Computational cost by training stage, on the original hardware of section 4.1.4.
X-ray unimodal candidates on the paired cohort: validation and test accuracy, quadratic weighted kappa and KL1 recall.
MRI unimodal candidates on the paired cohort: validation and test accuracy, quadratic weighted kappa and KL1 recall.
Traditional fusion operators on the test split. All three share the ConvNeXt V2 + SimSiam SSL branch pairing, so the comparison isolates the fusion operator.
Contrastive fusion on the test split, over the two-by-two grid of X-ray and MRI branches.
Residual-Calibrated Kalman Fusion on the test split, over the same two-by-two grid of branches as Table 4.8.
Ensemble and dynamic-routing results on the test split. Switch precision is 0.000 for the static ensembles because they never switch.
Oracle selection bounds on the test split: the ceiling a perfect per-sample router over each pool could reach. Not achievable.
Subject-clustered bootstrap point estimates and 95% confidence intervals on the test split, B = 2000 resamples.
Paired subject-clustered bootstrap: Fusion C-MODES minus each baseline, with 95% confidence intervals on the difference.
Quantisation-aware distilled student against the FP32 teacher on the test split, with the cost of quantisation as a signed difference.
